prediction.raw: <1> **Why:** As a Muslim, your grief is **completely valid and Islamically permissible**. Islam does not categorize natural human emotions like grief as "wrong." In fact, the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) himself wept openly when his son Ibrahim passed away, saying: > *"The eyes shed tears and the heart grieves, but we say only what pleases Allah."* (Sahih al-B Bukhari 130) Allah explicitly acknowledges human vulnerability in the Quran: > *"And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good news to the patient."* (Quran 2:155) Grief is part of the test of patience ( * sabr*), not a sin. This is not a " right or wrong" moral judgment—it’s a natural, faith-affirming response. May Allah grant you patience, strength, and comfort. Ameen. 💛
